author: ValWood
body:
* **PTHR ID & PTN node:**


GO:0019216 | regulation of lipid metabolic process | IBA with PTN000281649 , MGI:2686271 | GO_REF:0000033


* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**

https://www.pombase.org/gene/SPBC1703.11 and others

* **Type of Issue: Erroneous source or erroneous propagation, or other issue**

This annotation comes from a single paper descbiding ‘global metabolic’ rather than cell level phenotypes

https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22869679/
‘tissue level phenotypes Opa3(L122P) mice displayed an 80% reduction in insulin-like growth factor 1, postnatal growth retardation and hepatic steatosis. A 90% reduction in uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1) expression in interscapular BAT was accompanied by a marked reduction in surface body temperature, with a 2.5-fold elevation in interscapular BAT mass and lipid storage. The sequestration of circulating lipid into BAT resulted in profound reductions in epididymal and retroperitoneal WAT mass, without affecting subcutaneous WAT. The histological appearance and intense mitochondrial staining in intra-abdominal WAT suggest significant 'browning', but with UCP1 expression in WAT of Opa3(L122P) mice only 62% of that in wild-type littermates, any precursor differentiation does not appear to result in thermogenically active beige adipocytes. Thus, we have identified Opa3 as a novel regulator of lipid metabolism, coupling lipid uptake with lipid processing in liver and with thermogenesis in BAT. 


This 2023 review
https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0300908419302974?utm_source=chatgpt.com
on Secondary 3-methylglutaconic acidurias (3MGAs)
includes OPA3 and mentions possible roles which include 

“Interestingly, based on its [amino acid sequence](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/biochemistry-genetics-and-molecular-biology/peptide-sequence) and not function, OPA3 has been proposed to belong to the family of mitofusins like is OPA1 [[191](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0300908419302974?utm_source=chatgpt.com#bib191)]. Though OPA3 does not contribute to mitochondrial apoptosis, it might apparently potentiate it; on the other hand, its overexpression leads to mitochondria fragmentation whereas its deficiency leads to elongated mitochondria [[192](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0300908419302974?utm_source=chatgpt.com#bib192)].”

“The effects of OPA3 deficiency on [mitochondrial respiration](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/biochemistry-genetics-and-molecular-biology/mitochondrial-respiration) and ATP production are still currently controversial, some data arguing for mitochondrial metabolic dysfunction and reduced ATP synthesis on human permeabilized fibroblasts from Costeff patients [[61](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0300908419302974?utm_source=chatgpt.com#bib61)] and others for normal ATP formation in a model of Costeff syndrome [[29](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0300908419302974?utm_source=chatgpt.com#bib29)]. However, in this latter study, oxygen consumption was normal and most of the ATP was insensitive to the respiratory chain inhibitor [antimycin A](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/pharmacology-toxicology-and-pharmaceutical-science/antimycin-a), suggesting its glycolytic origin [[29](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0300908419302974?utm_source=chatgpt.com#bib29)].”

but do not mention a role in lipid metabolism, likely because lipid abnormailities can occur upstream or downstream of respiratory defects.


b) no known binding partners are known so difficult to couple uniquivocally to any specific mitochondiral pathway

A role in lipid metabolism can’t be ruled out but it isn’t highly supported so I would like to keep this as “unknown BP” and not propogate the annotation singe it’s quite weak.


* Add the label 'high priority' if needed. Generally high priority issues affect a lot of proteins, and annotations are incorrect (as opposed to just imprecise).
